critiques.target: Noise model (H4.1, H4.1.1, H1.1.3) and every kept/discarded verdict with |Δacc| < 0.3 pp
critiques.issue: E003 showed that runs are bit-reproducible, so run-to-run noise is zero. That makes the replicate useless as a noise floor. The noise that actually matters is trajectory noise: any code change re-rolls each seed's path. Its size, ~0.15-0.2 pp, was inferred from a single anecdote, seed 0 dropping 0.8 pp in E021. H4.1.1, the one experiment that would measure it, was never run. Meanwhile several verdicts rest on deltas inside that band: E012 'supports' H1.3.1 at -0.21 pp, E019 'refutes' H4.2.1 at -0.17 pp, E017 was kept at +0.16 pp, E020's +0.17 pp gain, E022's +0.09 pp, E014's +0.15 pp, and the E009 vs E010 ranking (a 0.18 pp difference).
critiques.suggestion: Run H4.1.1 now, since it costs only about 3×25 s. Take the E021 incumbent and run it with 3-4 different internal augmentation/data-order salts, holding the trial seeds fixed. Report the spread of the 3-seed mean. Then re-mark E012, E017, E019 and E020's accuracy gain as inconclusive (~) unless they clear about 2σ. From here on, any decision that hinges on a delta under 0.3 pp needs 2 salts.

critiques.target: Feasibility margin of the incumbent (E021, 0.7552) / H4
critiques.issue: All 23 experiments were selected on the same three fixed seeds (0, 1, 2). The tip is therefore winner's-cursed: the agent has been doing hill-climbing on those three trajectories. E020→E021 already showed the incumbent's mean regressing toward its seed median. A 0.22 pp margin over 0.753 is about one trajectory-noise σ, not the '~2.5σ' the notebook claims. H4 is also framed wrongly. The local gate is a fixed 3-seed mean ≥ 0.753, so lowering per-seed variance does not let you cut epochs. Its only real value is lower selection risk and better decisions.
critiques.suggestion: Outside the official run command, evaluate the incumbent on dev seeds 3-12 to estimate its true mean and std. If the dev mean is below about 0.754, treat further epoch trims as off-limits. Rewrite H4 as 'decision and selection noise limits progress', with the lever being replicates and dev seeds, not variance reduction.

critiques.target: H1.7.1 / the '~1 pp/s epoch exchange rate' used to score every per-step cut
critiques.issue: This rate came from E001→E002 (SGD, a different net) and from one Muon pair, E009→E014 (a 0.5-epoch step giving 0.44 pp, with about ±0.25 pp noise on the difference). E021's 0.25-epoch probe was too small to measure against trajectory noise, as the notebook itself admits. Every 'better than the epoch line' verdict therefore rests on a slope nobody has measured on the current graphed, progressive-resizing, batch-1536 recipe: E009, E010, E011, E013, E015 and E023.
critiques.suggestion: Measure the slope over a wide span on the E021 recipe, for example 9.25 → 10.25 → 11.25 total epochs, holding the low-res share fixed. Use 2 salts at each point. Re-score the old cuts against that line.

critiques.issue: The pp/s logic used to rescue resizing and the depth cut was not applied consistently. E013 cost 0.70 pp/s. That is better than the ~0.9-1 pp/s Muon epoch line the notebook later measured, and it would have been worth pairing with extra epochs, just as E011 was. It was dropped only because it missed the preregistered bound. H1.6 is still listed as 'open 0.15', which matches neither verdict.
critiques.suggestion: Once the slope has been re-measured, test a lighter filter on the incumbent (drop 10-15% in the last third of training) plus about 0.5 epoch. If it does not beat the new slope, set H1.6 to refuted. Either way, settle the status.

critiques.target: H1.5 evidence tokens and the E008 record
critiques.issue: E009+ and E010+ are cited for H1.5, but they test group-1 depth and width, not group-3 width. E008 is marked as refuting H1.5, yet it supports H1.5's Muon clause. E008's description also says 'lr 9.0, Lookahead, batch 1024' (SGD), while the outcome reports 213 steps at about 41 ms/step and compares against Muon E007. The record of what actually ran is inconsistent. Even read generously, 768 wide at 8.5 epochs scored -0.30 pp against 576 at 9.0 epochs. Correcting for 0.5 epoch (~0.45 pp), width was roughly +0.15 pp at equal epochs, with Muon lr not retuned. That is noise, not evidence that 'Muon makes full use of 576'.
critiques.suggestion: Fix the E008 description and move E009/E010 evidence over to H2.4. Set H1.5 to inconclusive. If width is revisited, do it on the current per-step cost structure (CUDA graph, batch 1536, resizing). Test group-2 or group-3 width at equal epochs with 2 salts, and do not combine it with an epoch cut.

critiques.issue: The results already contradict it. The profiler (E018/E023) shows non-conv kernels at about 23% of time, against the 40% predicted, and convs at about 18.6 of 24.5 ms. E008 showed that widening low-res layers is not 'nearly free' (+7% per step). E023 showed the next group-1 cut costs about 1.4 pp. What remains is the bare observation that 128-channel high-res convs cost more than their MAC share. Low tensor-core efficiency at small channel counts would explain that just as well as memory bandwidth.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H2.4.1 refuted and lower H2.4 to about 0.3, or rewrite it as 'high-resolution 128-channel convs run at low tensor-core utilization'. The rewritten version predicts that channel counts or layouts that improve cuDNN efficiency (for example channels in multiples of 64 or 128, a 3×3 vs 2×2 whitening stride) cut time. The current version predicts BN/GELU fusion would.

critiques.target: H1.7 (Muon recipe untuned, SGD-era parts are dead weight), open at 0.60
critiques.issue: Its core claim has been contradicted. Removing Lookahead plus the triangular warmup cost 0.52 pp (E016), batch 1024 lost on time (E022), and the Hiverge constants were only within noise (E017). E016 changed two things at once and kept lr 0.24 without warmup, so it cannot say which part helps. H1.7.5's premise, adding an LR floor, may already hold, since E019 says the LR decays to 0.07×. H1.7.4 (attribution) was never run and is now moot.
critiques.suggestion: Drop H1.7 to about 0.3 and retire H1.7.4. Check the actual end-of-schedule LR and retire H1.7.5 if a floor already exists. If the schedule is pursued, split E016: Lookahead off with the triangle kept. Lookahead costs nothing in time, so the only real upside is the schedule shape, plus a small Muon lr/momentum sweep at batch 1536, which has never been tuned for this net.

critiques.issue: The prediction said the mean would rise to ≥0.756. The result was 0.7482. Only the '≥0.4 pp rise' clause held, and the time bound was slightly missed. The verdict was taken from the one clause that hit.
critiques.suggestion: Set it to refuted or inconclusive. Retire the whole H1.1 SGD branch, since it never reached the target and Muon has superseded it.

critiques.target: Surprising result: E020 (resizing improved accuracy and cut time) vs E015 (resizing cost 0.43 pp)
critiques.issue: E020 gained +0.17 pp while saving 0.34 s, while E015's similar setup lost 0.43 pp. The usual explanation is the extra 0.5 epoch, the batch-1536 base, and seed 0's lucky 0.7623, which E021 suggests is part of it. A competing explanation was never tested: a FixRes-style effect, where training at low resolution and then finishing at 32 px helps in itself. The resizing schedule space is also barely explored. H2.3.1's proposed 24/28/32 three-stage schedule was never run, nor were a higher low-res share, 20 px, or a larger batch in the low-res phase (where fixed per-step Muon cost dominates).
critiques.suggestion: Resizing is the biggest lever measured so far (about -21% per epoch at 24 px), so sweep it. Try 6-7 low-res epochs out of 11-11.5, a 24/28/32 schedule, and batch 2048-3072 during the 24 px phase. Score against the re-measured slope, with 2 salts.

critiques.issue: The E018 profile named NS steps 3→2 (about -0.35 ms/step, ~1.5%) and Muon every k steps as the next per-step cuts. Neither was run. These are near-free in accuracy terms and stack with everything else. H3 is effectively exhausted: prepare is about 0.06 s and E018 removed the trial-1 excess, which supports H3.2.2, yet H3.2.2 is still 'open'.
critiques.suggestion: Run NS=2 on E021, judging time at about 0.5% noise and accuracy with salts. Close H3 at low priority: mark H3.2.2 supported via E018, and mark H3.2.1 supported via E006's zero recompiles.

critiques.target: Missing Lvl1: transfer to the official judging conditions
critiques.issue: No hypothesis covers the gap between local measurement and the official score. Judging uses an A100 PCIe (300 W cap, different clock behavior from the SXM) and 40 seeds. A change that wins 1-2% locally might not keep its ranking under power-capped clocks. The accuracy side is covered above.
critiques.suggestion: Add a low-confidence Lvl1 (or a note under H4) saying that small time wins (<2%) should be treated as provisional. Prefer cuts that remove work (steps, pixels, NS iterations) over cuts that depend on clock or kernel scheduling.

structured_output.summary: The biggest problem with this hypothesis tree is noise. Runs are bit-reproducible, but every code change re-rolls each seed's trajectory, which is worth about 0.15-0.2 pp. That figure comes from one anecdote and has never been measured: H4.1.1 was never run. Several verdicts sit inside that band: E012, E017, E019, E020's accuracy gain, E022, and the E009 vs E010 ranking. On top of that, all selection used the same three fixed seeds, so the incumbent's margin is winner's-cursed. E021 is only 0.22 pp above 0.753, about 1σ, not 2.5σ. The ~1 pp/s epoch exchange rate used to score every per-step cut comes from one SGD pair and one noisy Muon pair. It has never been measured on the current recipe. Applied consistently, it would have kept loss filtering (E013, 0.70 pp/s) alive rather than dropping it. Some hypotheses are still open with high confidence even though the results contradict them. H2.4's memory-bandwidth mechanism fails the profiler check (23% vs 40% non-conv time). H1.7's 'SGD-era parts are dead weight' fails E016 and E022. H1.5's evidence is misfiled, and E008's description doesn't match what ran. H1.1.2's 'supports' verdict was taken from one clause of the prediction. The most surprising result is E020: resizing improved accuracy while cutting time. Seed luck explains part of it, and a FixRes-style effect is untested. The resizing schedule is the largest proven lever and the least explored. Never tried: noise replicates, dev seeds 3-12, a wide-span epoch slope, NS 3→2, a three-stage 24/28/32 schedule or a larger low-res share or low-res batch, and the split Lookahead-only ablation. No Lvl1 covers transfer to the PCIe judging GPU and the 40-seed mean. Suggested next steps, in order: (1) salt replicates and dev seeds on E021; (2) a wide-span epoch slope; (3) NS=2; (4) a resizing-schedule sweep scored against the new slope.
